Dolaylı vergi: Taxes arising from the use of goods and services, paid by everyone at the same rate, independent of income or wealth.
Dolaysız vergi: Taxes paid periodically and by the taxpayer itself, depending on income or wealth.
Dolaşımdaki Banknotlar: The banknotes issued into circulation by the CBRT and in circulation.
Dolaşımdaki Para: The amount obtained by subtracting from the total of banknotes in circulation and coins the amounts of banknotes and coins held in bank vaults.
Dominant Position Test: The test taken into account in the evaluation of merger and acquisition transactions under the Competition Act. In the dominance test, a substantial lessening of competition occurs through the creation of a dominant position or the strengthening of an existing dominant position.
Doğal işsizlik oranı: Or in short UN: the lowest unemployment rate seen as a result of the normal functioning of the labor market and sustainable in the long run.
Doğal kaynak: Or land, in short N: the fundamental production factor denoting land that can be cultivated or built upon, as well as any kind of resource coming from the land and nature.
Doğal oran önsavı: The theoretical expectation that, whatever the inflation rate, the unemployment rate will return over time to its natural level.
Doğal tekel: A market structure in which, owing to increasing returns to scale, the lowest cost in production can be achieved with a single seller.
Doğrudan (Kesin) Alım: One of the open market operations the CBRT uses, within the framework of its monetary policy targets, with the aim of effectively regulating the money supply and the liquidity of the economy. It generally refers, in cases of a permanent liquidity shortage (tightness) in the market, to the CBRT's purchasing securities for its own portfolio from the market (from institutions authorized to conduct open market operations) and permanently providing liquidity to the system in return.
Doğrudan (Kesin) Satım: One of the open market operations the CBRT uses, within the framework of its monetary policy targets, with the aim of effectively regulating the money supply and the liquidity of the economy. It generally refers, in cases of a permanent liquidity surplus in the market, to the CBRT's selling securities from its own portfolio to the market (to institutions authorized to conduct open market operations) and permanently withdrawing the liquidity surplus from the system in return.
Doğrudan alım: The transaction of the central bank purchasing securities in the open market.
Doğrudan kotasyon: Or in short E: the exchange rate showing how much domestic currency can be bought in exchange for one unit of foreign currency.
Doğrudan müdahale: The practices by which the state influences the market through price or quantity regulation.
Doğrudan satım: The transaction of the central bank selling securities in the open market.
Doğrudan Yabancı Yatırım: A long-term form of investment in which the investor controls the management of an enterprise, or has a say in its management, in an economy other than the one where it is resident. In foreign direct investment, what is essential is that the investor holds a 10% or greater share in the enterprise's capital or has a say in its management.
Due Diligence: Due Diligence is the analysis containing all the necessary financial, legal and administrative information required for an investment decision to be made, showing the company's current situation and enabling the most accurate forecasts about its future. Fixed Assets: business assets that do not have the property of being converted into cash within one year.
Duopol: A market structure in which there are only two sellers of a good. Each producer generally has to take into account the other's reaction regarding any change it will make in price or production quantity. Since competition is between only two firms, their degrees of interdependence are quite high.
DuPont analizi: The analysis that breaks return on equity (ROE) into three components: ROE = Net Profit Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier. It shows which item is dragging down profitability; not fabricated terms like 'profit multiplier' or the like.
Duran varlık: Or fixed capital: durable goods such as machinery, factories, vehicles and buildings produced to generate income in the future.
Dâhilde İşleme Rejimi: An incentive system that grants customs exemption for the raw materials or inputs to be used in production and needing to be imported, on the condition of exporting. DASK: the Compulsory Earthquake Insurance that covers, in cash and within the limits stated in the policy, the material damage directly caused by an earthquake and the fire, explosion, tsunami and landslide resulting from it. Variable Expenses: expenses in a given accounting period that vary (increase or decrease) according to production volume. Foreign Trade: a state's foreign
Dönemsel Faiz: Refers to the interest an investment will yield over the period it is actually held.
Dördüncü derece fiyat ayrımcılığı: Or reverse price discrimination: the practice of selling a given product to each buyer at the same price even though its cost differs for different buyers.
Döviz: The currencies of foreign countries or any payment instruments substituting for foreign currency.
Döviz arz eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the exchange rate and the quantity of foreign currency supplied, all else being constant.
Döviz arzı: Or in short SE: the total quantity of foreign currency that all units in the economy want to sell, depending on the exchange rate, in a given period.
Döviz Kuru: The expression of one national currency in terms of another national currency.
Döviz kuru hedeflemesi: A monetary policy regime in which the central bank targets a fixed exchange rate or a band between the national currency and another country's currency.
Döviz kuru istikrarı: The value of a country's currency remaining constant over time against other countries' currencies, or changing at a low and predictable rate.
Döviz Kuru Rejimleri: Today, owing to the importance they carry, particularly for small and open economies, and their potential to directly affect the real economy, exchange rates are used directly as target, indicator or instrument within the framework of the monetary policy implemented. Exchange rate practices take shape between two regimes: the fixed exchange rate regime at one end and free floating at the other. Under a fixed exchange rate regime, the value of the national currency is pegged against a foreign currency or a basket of currencies, and the maintenance of this value is guaranteed by the monetary authority, sometimes explicitly and sometimes implicitly. In Currency Board-type arrangements, while the rate is pegged on the one hand, on the other hand the national money supply is tied entirely to the foreign currency purchases and sales conducted at this rate. Under a free floating exchange rate regime, the price of the exchange rate is determined according to the supply and demand forming in the market. Besides these, many intermediate regimes exist. For example, under a floating regime the rate is largely determined by market supply and demand conditions, but the monetary authority intervenes in the market rarely and in limited amounts; under a managed float regime, again there is no exchange rate target, but interventions can occur frequently for various reasons. Under regimes known as the crawling peg, the rate is guided according to a set of criteria and is intervened in by the monetary authority when necessary. The choice of such exchange rate regimes varies according to the conditions countries find themselves in.
Döviz piyasası: The physical or virtual environment where the currencies of different countries are bought and sold, and where exchange rates are determined in this process.
Döviz piyasası dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of foreign currency demanded in the market equals the quantity supplied.
Döviz talebi: Or in short DE: the total quantity of foreign currency that all units in the economy want to purchase, depending on the exchange rate, in a given period.
Döviz talep eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the exchange rate and the quantity of foreign currency demanded, all else being constant.
Dünya Bankası: An international organization established after 1944 under the name 'International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)' for the reconstruction of Europe. It mainly provides long-term project credits to developing countries. In recent years, the concepts of developing countries' external debts and the fight against poverty have also entered its mandate.
Düzenleyici ve Denetleyici Kurumlar Bütç: The budget of the boards and superior boards established by special law, such as the Capital Markets Board, the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency, and the Radio and Television Supreme Council.
Düzeyi: The level of development determined by taking into account the economic, social, cultural, etc. criteria of a country, province or district. Start-up: the name given to innovative and risky ventures with rapid growth potential.
Düşük işsizlik: The low rate of unemployment — defined as persons who are seeking work but are not employed — within the labor force of a country.
Düşük mal: Products whose demand in the market decreases when the average income level rises.
Dış borç: The total amount of debt the state has received from households and firms resident abroad, or from other states.
Dış dünya: All the other countries with which an economy trades and establishes economic relations.
Dış Ticaret Dengesi: Expresses the difference between the amounts of goods exports and imports carried out between persons resident domestically and persons resident abroad, passing through customs. If exports exceed imports, a foreign trade surplus forms; in the opposite case, a foreign trade deficit forms.
Dış Ticaret Hadleri: The ratio of the export unit value index to the import unit value index. The terms of trade being above 100 shows that the export prices of the goods subject to foreign trade are higher than their import prices. Unit value indices are calculated by TUIK.
Dışa Bağımlılık: In countries that fall short of establishing their own technology and industrial infrastructure, the meeting of the investment goods, raw materials or intermediate goods required for production by importing them from other countries; the inability to produce the said materials and raw materials domestically.
Dışlama etkisi: The situation of the state's consumption and investment expenditures taking the place of private consumption and investments.
Dışlanabilirlik: Or excludability in consumption: the possibility of preventing persons who have not purchased a good or service from using that good or service.
Dışsallık: The effect an economic activity has on persons who are not party to that activity.
Dışsallıkların içselleştirilmesi: The methods that will ensure that economic units take social costs and benefits into account when making choices.
E-İhracat: The fulfillment of the shipment as Micro Export, by issuing an invoice (VAT-free) on behalf of the individual customer for a foreign-addressed order received through the e-commerce/online (internet) sales channel. E-Commerce: the conducting of commerce online in the digital environment. E-TUYS: the Electronic Incentive Application and Foreign Capital Information System, a web-based application in which the affairs and transactions relating to the investment incentive certificate, managed by the Directorate General for Incentive Implementation and Foreign Capital, are carried out.
Economies of Scope: If the cost of producing two products together is smaller than the sum of the cost of a firm producing only product x and the cost of a firm producing only product y, the existence of economies of scope is spoken of.
